newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers to build sorting office in Angola.
newsitem.headline: De Beers to build sorting office in Angola.

text.p: De Beers Consolidated Mines said it had signed an agreement with Angola's state diamond company Endiama to build a diamond sorting office in the capital Luanda this year, a company official said on Friday.
Director of De Beers' Central Selling Organisation (CSO) Gareth Penny told Reuters the office would sort and value Angola's diamond production estimated at two million carats annually.

"We have signed heads of agreement with Endiama...to build a sorting office of about 12 storeys. We are optimistic about signing the substantive agreement shortly and that is the last remaining hurdle," Penny told Reuters.

He said the project would be funded entirely by De Beers at a total cost of about $30 million. This is in addition to an estimated $50 million the mining giant is committed to under diamond prospecting agreements with Endiama it signed last year.
The company also loaned another $50 million to Endiama in 1991 to develop diamond resources in the Cuango River valley which produces annually around 1.5 million carats.
"We will sort and value Angola's diamond production. It will be designed to accommodate other production as well," Penny said.
"We believe this is important for Angola. If it is to benefit, as it should, from its diamond reserves and resources it should be controlled properly," Penny said.
He said de Beers would import its technology for the sorting of diamonds to Angola and set up training programmes as of June.

"We believe it is important that this master sample and the government diamond valuator protects the producer and gives him fair value, thereby generating significant foreign exchange reserves for the country.

"It is a controllable system that has worked extremely well in neighbouring countries such as Namibia, Botswana and South Africa," he said, adding that construction of the building would probably start in July and take up to 18 months to complete.

De Beers has signed five-year agreements with Endiama to search for diamonds in three areas -- the northeastern Lunda Norte province, Quela in Malange province and near Mavinga in the southern Cuando Cubango province.
